core_obligations: For a minimal prime q of the support of M use that M_q has finite length, so that the injective endomorphisms phi and psi become isomorphisms after localising (proof lines 17383-17387).
Conclude that the support of M/phi psi M is the closed point of A, hence that M/phi psi M has finite length (proof lines 17388-17389).

Verify exactness of the (2, 1)-periodic complex: the kernel of phi on M/phi psi M is psi M/phi psi M, so the kernel of phi equals the image of psi, and the symmetric statement for psi follows because M/phi psi M = M/psi phi M by the commuting-image hypothesis (proof lines 17390-17394).
proof_roadmap: Localise at a minimal prime of the support to get finite length there and isomorphisms (proof lines 17383-17387).
Read off that the support of the quotient is the closed point, giving finite length (proof lines 17388-17389).
Check the two kernel conditions directly (proof lines 17390-17394).
difficulty_reason: For a finite module M of dimension one over a Noetherian local ring A and two injective endomorphisms phi, psi with phi(psi(M)) = psi(phi(M)) - for instance commuting endomorphisms - the lemma asserts that M/phi psi M has finite length and that (M/phi psi M, phi, psi) is an exact (2, 1)-periodic complex (statement lines 17370-17380). The proof localises at a minimal prime q of the support of M, where M_q has finite length and both endomorphisms consequently become isomorphisms, so the support of M/phi psi M is concentrated at the closed point and hence has finite length (proof lines 17383-17389). Exactness is then checked directly: the kernel of phi on M/phi psi M is visibly psi M/phi psi M, so the kernel of phi is the image of psi, and the symmetric statement follows from the hypothesis M/phi psi M = M/psi phi M (proof lines 17390-17394). Recognising that injectivity plus the commuting-image condition is exactly what makes the two kernel computations match is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
